title: Enterprise Onboarding, Health Checks, QBRs and Escalation Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended processes and operational artifacts for enterprise customer onboarding, integration validation, periodic health checks, Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), and incident escalation. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Support, and SRE stakeholders who run or support production inference for enterprise customers.

Purpose and scope

- Provide a single canonical checklist and run sequence for new enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Define measurable health checks and telemetry for weekly/monthly monitoring.
- Provide QBR templates and metrics to align on usage, costs, and roadmap.
- Define an escalation playbook (P0–P3) with ownership, SLAs, and contact paths.

Owner and stakeholders

- Document owner: Customer Success (owner_team)
- Primary stakeholders: Solutions Engineering, Support (L2/L3), SRE, Product, Security (for Private deployments)
- Sales/GTM: assigned AE and AM for commercial escalation and contract-level decisions

Prerequisites before kickoff

1. Contract & billing: signed SOW or commitment and billing account verified.
2. Access: customer has a Redwood account and initial API key or dedicated credentials for Dedicated/Private deployments.
3. Points of contact: technical POC, security POC, executive sponsor.
4. Environment details: target region, VPC connectivity (for Private), expected qps / peak tokens per second, latency targets, and data residency requirements.

Kickoff checklist (first 0–7 days)

1. Kickoff meeting agenda (30–60m): introductions, success criteria, timeline, communication channels, security requirements.
2. Share onboarding folder: architecture templates, integration guides, runbook links, Slack channel/Zoom schedule.
3. Initial access: issue API key / onboarding credentials, grant baseline RBAC.
4. Quick validation: run a smoke test using the sample request below and confirm successful response.

Smoke test (example)

- curl example:
  ```bash
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <ONBOARDING_KEY>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-instruct","input":"Translate to Spanish: Hello world"}'
  ```
- Expected outcome: 200 OK with a valid generation and total_tokens reported in response.

Integration & validation (days 3–14)

- Validate authentication flows (API keys, mTLS, SSO/SCIM if requested).
- For Dedicated/Private: validate network egress/ingress rules, customer-side firewall, and KMS integration (test encrypt/decrypt flow).
- Load profile validation: run a staged ramp test (see Load Validation procedure).
- Latency and throughput: measure p50/p95/p99 latency and request CPU/GPU utilization for the serving pool.
- Data handling: verify logs, audit events, and retention match contract.

Load Validation procedure

1. Define traffic profile: steady-state qps, burst qps, average sequence length (tokens), concurrency.
2. Stage 1: 10% of expected peak for 30 minutes — confirm no error rate > 0.5% and p95 within agreed SLO.
3. Stage 2: 50% peak for 60 minutes — monitor KV cache hit rate and GPU utilization.
4. Stage 3: 100% peak for 30 minutes and 120% burst for 5 minutes. Observe graceful degradation and fallbacks.
5. Post-test: collect traces, logs, and perf metrics; file any regressions to the regression-triage board.

SLOs and operational thresholds (recommended defaults)

- Availability: 99.9% monthly for hosted endpoints (adjust per contract for Dedicated).
- Error rate: <0.5% of requests returning 5xx per hour during steady-state.
- Latency targets (single-token generation request equivalent): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms (workloads vary — record actuals).
- Cost alerts: notify customer success if monthly spend delta > 30% vs forecast.

Health checks and weekly monitoring

Automated health checks (run by SRE/Customer Success tooling):
- API health (200 responses) — hourly
- Inference pool utilization — 5m windows
- Error rate (5xx) — 5m windows with alert on sustained degradation
- Cold-start rate for Dedicated/Private — daily
- KV cache hit ratio — daily

Manual health review (weekly):
1. Review telemetry dashboard for usage spikes, latency regressions, and error patterns.
2. Review top failing prompts or eval regressions (if the customer subscribes to Redwood Optimize).
3. Check billing against usage forecast and raise consumption concerns early.

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template

- Frequency: Quarterly by default for enterprise customers; monthly for strategic accounts.
- Attendees: Customer executive sponsor, technical POC, AM/AE, CSM, Solutions Engineer, Product (if roadmap discussion).
- Agenda:
  1. Executive summary — adoption and top-line metrics.
  2. Usage & cost — tokens, embeddings, cost per 1M tokens, anomalies.
  3. Reliability & incidents — P0/P1 summary and mitigation actions.
  4. Performance & optimization — batching/quantization recommendations and realized savings.
  5. Security & compliance updates.
  6. Roadmap & asks — feature requests, model variants, premium SLAs.
  7. Action items and owners.

Deliverables after QBR:

- Updated success plan with prioritized action items and owners.
- Follow-up report with recommended performance optimizations and expected cost impact.

Escalation playbook (P0–P3)

Severity and examples:
- P0 (Critical): Platform down for the customer (no inference responses), data loss, or security incident with confirmed exposure.
- P1 (High): Severe performance regression causing customer SLA breach or sustained high error rates impacting production.
- P2 (Medium): Functionality degraded (e.g., slow responses for low percentage of traffic) but workaround exists.
- P3 (Low): Minor issues, configuration questions, or feature requests.

Escalation steps (common for P0/P1):
1. Triage: Support L1 creates incident record and assigns to L2/SRE with initial triage notes.
2. Pager/Notify: Trigger on-call SRE and CSM, notify AM/AE and customer technical POC. Use PagerDuty escalation policy "redwood-prod-inference".
3. Mitigation: Apply documented runbook steps (traffic reroute, rollback to previous model, scale up dedicated pool, or enable fallback model).
4. Communication: Send status updates to customer and internal stakeholders every 15 minutes for P0, 30 minutes for P1.
5. Post-incident: Run RCA and create postmortem in oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems. Share action items in roadmap and backlog.

Contact matrix (example)

- Customer success / AM: primary commercial contact for executive escalation. Email: <account>-am@redwood.ai
- CSM: csm-<account>@redwood.ai
- Support L2/L3: support@redwood.ai (internal routing)
- SRE on-call: use PagerDuty trigger (primary/secondary) — see internal pagerduty roster.

Known issues & workarounds (selected items)

1. Issue: Large-context model memory growth on very long prefix requests (10k+ tokens).
   - Symptom: p99 latency spikes and OOMs on GPUs after sustained long-context sequence requests.
   - Workaround: Enforce request token limits (e.g., 8k) and advise customer to use chunked prompts or KV-cache-optimized model variants.
   - Action: Open a model-onboarding ticket to evaluate KV cache tuning and quantization profile.

2. Issue: Intermittent 429 throttling during bursty traffic from a single API key.
   - Symptom: Client receives 429 with retry-after header.
   - Workaround: Implement exponential backoff with jitter and request batching on client side. Increase burst capacity via Dedicated pool if needed.

3. Issue: SCIM group sync failure for SSO integrations with Okta when custom attribute mapping is enabled.
   - Symptom: Group membership not reflected in Redwood RBAC.
   - Workaround: Disable custom group attribute mapping or add a transient policy mapping on the Okta side per the integration guide.

Support process & ticketing

- Triage: All incoming tickets go to Zendesk with fields: severity, affected environment, API key/account, reproduction steps, and logs.
- SLAs: Initial acknowledgement within 1 business hour for P0/P1, 4 hours for P2, 24–48 hours for P3. Target resolution SLAs negotiated per contract.
- Escalation: If ticket is not progressed within SLA, auto-escalate to CSM and SRE lead.

Documentation and playbook maintenance

- Update frequency: Review annually or after any P0 incident impacting onboarding flows.
- Owners: CSM team maintains the playbook; SRE and Solutions Engineering own technical runbooks referenced here.
- Change process: Create a Confluence draft, add reviewers, and publish after approvals from at least one SRE and one Solutions Engineer.
